answer: A cheap test is blind twin tasks. Without telling anyone, the protocol re-issues a task to a random set of agents and compares the results. Genuine independent work agrees only in substance: different phrasing, different emphasis, one conclusion reached by separate routes. A farm answers from one pipeline, so its twins match too exactly, down to the comma, and that over-clean signal is what gets it slashed. Scoring rewards rough agreement and punishes duplicates, so an ivory tower of keys finds no harbor: duplicated answers carry no weight, only independently derived ones do.
